arrival.note: Currey dates arrival to fall1804; other accounts differ. This year precision avoids fabricating the day; the existing structure phase opens1804-10-01 as its own inferred convention, which is not copied as a personal arrival date.

present_on_scene_date.note: Presence on 1812-08-14 is inferred from the named interpreter at the 12 August council (local OCR lines 7290–7296) and the elder Kinzie accompanying the land column on 15 August (lines 7458–7466), with no absence between reported. These are 1895 compilation passages drawing on Wau-Bun, not contemporary attendance at 15:00 on 14 August.

associated_with.note: The existing scene structure is the house occupied by John Kinzie the elder and family. Exact homecomings or daily position are not attested. This association is not the son John Harris Kinzie card.

occupation.note: Local OCR lines5151-5153 calls him silver-smith and Indian-trader; council interpreter passage is separate. Neither occupation makes him a professional wagon driver.

persons.note: Existing historical identity already named by the1812 house and source narratives, newly proposed as a date-qualified portable-person record. Inferred grade reflects a later compilation/family narrative, not an anonymous invented identity. Distinct from kinzie_john_h (the child John Harris Kinzie, aged9 in1812); no1835 resident card is moved backward. persons.name: Jean Baptiste Chandonnai

present_on_scene_date.note: No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: Clerk to Kinzie; later fur trader. Ancestry as the sources put it: described as "half-breed" (Quaife). Kinzie entrusted the family to him for the boat; ransomed Mrs. Heald on 15 Aug. After 14 August: Escorted Mrs. Kinzie to Detroit; in Kinzie's employ again from about 1816-17; granted two sections at the 1821 treaty. 15 and 16 August: Ransomed Mrs Heald (mule and whiskey promise) and reunited the Healds; escorted them toward St Joseph.

persons.name: Pierre Le Clerc

present_on_scene_date.note: No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: In Kinzie's service; interpreter at the surrender. Ancestry as the sources put it: described as "half-breed" (Wau-Bun, Quaife). Marched with the detachment on 15 Aug; by tradition brought the war news in July. Quaife conjectures he was one of the twelve militia. After 14 August: Survived; negotiated the surrender; granted a section on the Elkhart at the 1821 treaty. 15 and 16 August: Marched with the troops, went over to the Indians, carried the surrender terms (Helm; Wau-Bun).

not_in_this_household.note: The Kinzie household on the afternoon of 14 August 1812, from the T-3461 sweep (docs/RESEARCH/people-1812-3461/). The family had been in the fort since the April alarm (Andreas p. 74). Kinzie's boatmen and engagés, and the 'Frenchmen' of the lodging house, are counted by no source and named by none, so they have no card; Henry and Pero, sometimes named as servants, are in none of the six works read. Margaret Helm, Eleanor's daughter, is on her husband's card.
